newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield rises to 21.40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield rises to 21.40 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 47 basis points to 21.40 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 80 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 20.94 percent coupon for a price of 99.7954 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 20.93 percent.

The bank also sold 30 billion bolivars of 268-day notes with a 21.48 percent coupon at a price of 98.6026 percent, and 30 billion bolivars of 359-day notes with a 22.04 percent coupon at an average price of 97.7297 percent.
Yields for these notes rose 64 basis points to 23.69 percent for 268-day bills, and 75 basis points to 24.88 percent for the 359-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
